construct: After birth, erythroid BCL11A acts as a potent transcriptional repressor of the fetal gamma-globin genes, promoting the developmental switch from HbF (alpha2gamma2) toward adult beta-globin-containing hemoglobin. Reduced BCL11A activity derepresses gamma-globin and increases HbF.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: The normal postnatal decline in gamma-globin requires fetal hemoglobin silencing; BCL11A is a major erythroid repressor of gamma-globin and a key regulator of the HbF-to-HbA switch.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Other listed transcription factors regulate important cellular programs but none is the canonical erythroid gamma-globin silencer whose knockdown preserves HbF.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: Developmental gamma-to-beta switching plus experimental preservation of HbF uniquely identifies BCL11A.
